court: In the High Court of Madras
prayer: PRAYER: This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, against the decree and judgment dated 28.11.2012 passed in MCOP No. 51 of 2010 by the Subordinate Judge, Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal, Harur.
judgment_text:
The Judgment of the Court was delivered by

V. Bhavani Subbaroyan, J.:— The appellant is the claimant in MCOP No. 51 of 2010 on the file of the Subordinate Judge, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Harur and she filed the present appeal challenging the decree and judgment passed in the above said claim petition seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. The case of the claimant/appellant is as follows.

On 30.05.2007, the claimant and her husband, mother-in-law and relatives were traveling in a Maruthi Versa Car bearing registration No. TN-29-AZ 5859 belonging to the first respondent and insured with the 2nd respondent. At about 4.00 a.m, when the car was nearing Hindustan Petroleum Bunk, Kodai Road, the driver of the car bearing registration No. TN-29-AZ-5859 drove the vehicle rashly and negligently and dashed against the parking lorry bearing registration No. KA-01-AD-6995, as a result of which, the claimant and other members sustained grievous injuries and they were admitted in Rajeswari Hospital in Dindukkal. The further case of the claimant is that for better treatment, she was admitted as inpatient from 30.05.2007 to 23.08.2007 in Apollo Specialty Hospitals, Madurai and had spent several lakhs of rupees for treatment. Hence, she filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs. 20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in the above said road accident.

3. Before Tribunal, the first respondent remained absent and was set exparte and the 2nd respondent contested the claim petition.

4. In the Trial Court, on the side of the claimant, the claimant and Dr. P. Ramakrishan were examined as PW1 and PW2 and Ex.P1 to Ex.P15 were marked. On the side of the respondents, no oral and documentary evidence was adduced.

5. After analysing the evidence on record, the learned Subordinate Judge, Motor Accident claims Tribunal, Harur awarded a sum of Rs. 9,57,600/- as compensation.

6. Not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed the present appeal for enhancement of compensation on the following grounds.

(i) The trial court has erred in awarding only a sum of Rs. 1,29,600/-, towards “Partial permanent disability”, when the claimant had suffered 4 fractures on her neck.

(ii) Without considering the fact that the claimant had spent more than Rs. 10,00,000/- for medical expenses alone, the trial court has awarded a very meager amount of Rs. 9,57,500/- as compensation and hence, the same is liable to be enhanced.

7. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant contended that due to the accident, the claimant had sustained grievous injuries on her cervical spinal cord and she had been treated as inpatient from 30.05.2007 to 23.8.2007 in the Apollo Specialty Hospital, Madurai and had spent several lakhs of rupees for treatment. He further contended that the claimant is not in a position to do her routine work, without any assistant and she is not able to stand, walk, sit for long time and move frequently. His further contention is that on account of cervical injury sustained by the claimant, she had lost her earning capacity and she is not able to do any work as is done before the accident and hence he prayed that the compensation awarded by the tribunal has got to be enhanced.

8. A perusal of the discharge summary (Ex.P4) shows that the claimant was unable to move all 4 limbs, since the time of accident and sensations absent including perianal region, which reflexes absent on all 4 limbs, cervical spine tenderness. The further contentions stated in the Ex.P4 is extracted hereunder.

Discussion: 20 years old Mrs. Kousalya was admitted with alleged history of RTA on 30.05.2007 white traveling in a 4 wheeler. She was quadoplegic on arrival and MRI Spine showed C4/5 fracture with facet dislocation and cord contusion. She was taken up for C3-6 posterior spinal fusion with titanium rods, sublaminar wring with disc bend grafting GA on 02.06.2007. Post operatively she responded well to treatment and improved neurologically with physiotherapy. She is being is charged with advice to continue the same at home/rehabilitation centre.

Condition on discharge: Afebrile; Upper limb Power: G III Proximally, G II Distally: Lower limb: Grade 4 on the right side and grade 4 on the left side: Able to sit on chair and stand with support; She is on normal diet an continuous bladder drainage.

9. Dr. P. Ramarkrishnan, who has given disability certificate (Ex.P12) has assessed the disability of the claimant as 65%. In Ex.P12, he has stated as follows.

“Continuous back ache at lumbar region and the MRI showed post disk protrusion at L4 L5 and S1 level causing Foremetimal narrowing.

“Because of those injuries, now the patient has Gr.III Mealoness of RT upper limb Distial Prosimal

Gr. II mealoness of left upper limb Distal Proximally

Finger: 0 to 1 + with contractions of fingers and hard grips not possible

Both upper limbs are spastic.

Lower limbs: Right Gr.II to Gr.III Proximal Distal

Left Gr.II to Gr.I Distal Proximal, spastic limbs LT.

Patient can mobilised on wheel chair only and able to stand with support and not able to walk. She is totally depended on others for her daily routine requirements and basic needs.

10. The PW2 has assessed the partial permanent disability suffered by the claimant as 65%. However, the Tribunal has reduced the same as 20%, without assigning any acceptable reason. Hence, this court fixed the partial permanent disability as 65%, based on the evidence of medical records. The Tribunal has rightly fixed the monthly income of the claimant as Rs. 3,000/- per month and had adopted proper multiplier ‘18’. Therefore, partial permanent disability is calculated as follows

3,000 × 12 × 65% × 18 - Rs. 4,21,200

11. As far as the other heads are concerned, the Tribunal had rightly awarded a sum of Rs. 4,70,000/- towards medical bills as per Ex.P5 and a sum of Rs. 3,51,000/- towards medical bills as per Ex.P10 and Ex.P11. However, a very meagre amount of Rs. 5,000 and Rs. 2,000 towards “pain and sufferings” and “Extra Nourishment” respectively. Considering the injuries suffered by the claimant, the same is enhanced to Rs. 25,000 and Rs. 5,000/- respectively, In addition to that, a sum of Rs. 2,500/- is awarded towards “transportation charges”.

12. The revised award passed under various heads by this court is extracted hereunder.

13. In the result,

i) The appeal is allowed in part. No costs. The quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal is enhanced to Rs. 12,74,700/- from Rs. 9,57,600/-.

ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs. 12,74,700/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit.

iii) The 2nd respondent/National Insurance Company Limited is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs. 12,74,700/- along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum, less the amount already deposited by them, within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

iv) On such deposit being made by the 2nd respondent/Insurance company, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the entire amount, after following due process of law.
